lessons.content: Bash (Bourne Again Shell) is a command language interpreter that executes commands read from the standard input or from a file. It's the default shell on most Linux distributions and macOS.
objectives: Understand what Bash is and its purpose
lessons.example_explanation: The shebang (#!/bin/bash) tells the system which interpreter to use. The echo command prints text to the terminal.
exercises: Create a script that prints your name
Add comments to explain what your script does
tips: Always start your bash scripts with #!/bin/bash

lessons.title: Variables and Data Types
lessons.content: Variables in bash are used to store data. Unlike other programming languages, bash variables don't have explicit data types - everything is treated as a string by default.
objectives: Learn how to declare and use variables
lessons.code_example:
#!/bin/bash

# Variable declaration
name="John"
age=25

# Using variables
echo "Name: $name"
echo "Age: $age"

# Variable concatenation
full_info="$name is $age years old"
echo $full_info
lessons.example_explanation: Variables are assigned without spaces around the = sign. Use $ to access variable values. Variables can be concatenated within double quotes.
exercises: Create variables for your favorite color, number, and food
Display them in a formatted message
tips: No spaces around = when assigning variables
Use double quotes to preserve spaces in variable values
